lines.en: I knock on Io’s door and wait for her to answer.
But several seconds go by without a response and, given that she doesn’t normally work this late, I start to wonder if she might be out doing something else.
But then I remember that this is Io we’re talking about, and that the likelihood of her actually doing anything other than working or hanging out in her room is practically zero.
So I knock again.
: Hey. Are you in there?
Time starts to tick by and-
: Ngh...what?
: Sensei?
: Is that you?
: Did I wake you up?
: Not...exactly but...
: Can I come in?
: Yeah...Let me just get this out of the way and-
: Ah!
Something falls over and hits the ground.
But considering there are roughly six million objects inside of Io’s room, things like this are bound to happen.
I’ll have to ask Ami to clean this room while Io is away since Uta is clearly incapable of fulfilling her maidly duties and-
: Ngh...
: Are you okay?
: Was that you who fell just now?
: ...Probably.
: I feel like that’s something you should know.
: Just...a little out of it...
: So, uhh...
: What’s up?
: What’s up is you’re either extremely tired or extremely drunk.
: Or extremely messed up from mixing medications and not eating anything all day.
: Medication?
: It’s the fancy word for medicine.
: I know what it means, Io.
: Cool. Then we can forget this happened and talk about something else.
: The next time you don’t respond to my knocks, I’m just walking away.
: If you need rest or whatever, you shouldn’t be getting out of bed for me.
: I told you, I’m good. Just a little out of it.
: This isn’t like, an abnormal thing. It happens all the time and it’s easily preventable.
: I’m just a little dizzy.
: Can you stand?
: Probably not. So if we could hang out on the ground, that would be cool.
: I mean...that doesn't exactly sound like a good time. But I don’t think it can be helped at this point.
: If you’re okay with catching me, I can try standing up.
: You weigh probably just as much as my cell phone, so that much wouldn’t be a problem.
: But I don’t think you should be overexerting yourself if you’re sick.
: I’m not sick sick. I’m Io sick.
: Is that some new form of debilitating disease?
: Yeah. They made it just for me.
: Really, though. What’s wrong?
: It’s a secret.
: You hate secrets.
: The pill bottles are right behind me and I’m in no shape to fight you.
: I mean, even if I wasn’t all messed up right now, I wouldn’t be in any shape to fight you. You’re really big.
: But go ahead and read them if you’re that curious. There are some pretty wild names on there.
: Oh, and there are a couple more under the bed you can probably find if you lay down and move your arm around.
: They fell off the mini fridge when I tried to make it to the door and now I'm gonna have to crawl under there and get them back.
: I’d really prefer if you’d just tell me what's wrong so I don’t have to Google some complicated name that I won't even be able to say out loud.
: I mean, if it was just one thing, I wouldn’t have so many different bottles, right?
: I’m all sorts of broken. I already told you this.
: You don’t look that broken to me.
: And you don’t look that broken to me. So we’re either really good at judging each other or really bad at it.
: Why are you still standing?
: Because I don’t want you to throw up on me.
: I’m not going to throw up on you.
: Well, I probably would if you like, spun me around or something. But that’s not a thing you’ve done so far, so unless you’ve developed some weird new hobby...
: Spinning isn’t really an interest of mine. But I could pick you up and put you down on your bed if you want to get some rest.
: Oooooooor...we could use the kotatsu I just fixed so you don’t have to throw me over a bunch of obstacles and risk knocking the rest of my stuff down.
: It also gives us an excuse for me to lay on your lap and have you pat my head.
: What if you’re not sick at all and this is just one elaborate ploy to obtain a lap pillow?
: Then I am a much better actor than I thought I was.
: Io-
: Come oooooooon. It’s really warm under there. And I’m super light. You won’t even know I’m on you.
: I have no problem with you being “on” me. I’m just having a hard time telling you that I think we should maybe talk about all of these medications.
: Are you a doctor?
: I’m not.
: Well then what good will talking about my medications do for either of us?
: I’m fine. I’ve got a bunch of stuff that I can take for certain things whenever I need to take them.
: I just happened to need several different things tonight and, mixed with the fact that I haven’t eaten at all and how I barely slept last night-
: Boom. Down goes Io.
: Hah...
I sigh to myself and accept that Io’s probably not going to give me any specific details tonight.
But I think it’s pretty safe to assume that it’s nothing physical if she only takes them when she needs to and-
Well, I guess they could still technically be painkillers or something.
Damn it.
Why did she have to pick now to get all light headed?
I turn off the lights before moving over to the kotatsu and sliding myself underneath it.
Io waits on her step ladder until I’m in place and then very slowly and clumsily climbs onto me, resting her body in my lap and her head on my chest.
It’s a position that makes me acutely aware that I must focus at least half of my energy on not getting an erection because it would be overwhelmingly apparent to her if I did.
I stabilize myself with my left hand and use my right one to softly rub her shoulder.
It’s not something I’d normally have any interest in doing, but...given the context of the situation, I think it’s okay for me to be a little nice.
At least until she’s able to stand on her own two feet again.
As soon as that happens, she can rub her own shoulder.
: Guh...sleepy...
: One of the downsides to pretty much every single anxiety medication is how tired they make you.
Ahh, so it wasn't anything physical.
Shocker.
: You have anxiety?
: Amongst other things.
: Was the anxiety part not obvious to you?
: I probably could have guessed. It just sounded rude to say something like, “I thought so.”
: Well, thank you for your sudden increase in generosity.
: Maybe I should just always invite you over before I take my meds to reap the benefits of being your student.
: What’s with the emphasis on “your?”
: There aren’t many teachers who would let an anxious, loopy, drugged out [teenager] climb into their lap.
: Yeah. Ms. Watabe would have never let you do this with her.
: Good. Because I wouldn’t want to do this with Ms. Watabe.
: You, on the other hand...
: I could do this every night for the rest of my life and not get tired of it.
: Io?
: Yeah?
: Why do you like me so much?
: Because I have to.
: Why?
: Because you’re my last bastion of hope for adults in this world.
: I am so tired of everyone else that if things don’t work out with you, I’ll probably just die.
: Oh, okay. That doesn’t put all of the pressure in the world on my shoulders or anything.
: You’ve already got the rest of me weighing down on you. Might as well go for the shoulders, too.
: That was kind of just a joke anyway.
: You really are my last line of defense, though.
: And probably the only example of something that I’ve wanted that I’ve actually made a push for.
: Some push you’re making, nearly passing out in front of me.
: There have been other pushes. This one was just a convenient coincidence.
: If I’m being completely honest, Sensei...I don’t know why it was you who appealed to me.
: You were probably just in the right place at the right time.
: So it could have been anyone?
: It could have been anyone.
: But...
: I’m glad it was you.
: Uta’s home!
: Welcome back. Don’t mind us.
: Uta’s not home! Please carry on!
: Wait, no. Stay.
: I want you here.
: Uhh...
: Pleeeeeease?
: I...don’t know...
: Like...this seems like something I probably shouldn’t get involved in...
: I think you’re misunderstanding the situation.
: Did you take too much again?
: Oh. Or you completely understand the situation.
: After a few seconds of actually thinkin’ about it, yeah.
: How are you feeling? Do you need any water? Juice?
: I’m okay now that Sensei’s letting me use his lap.
: Good...I’m glad...
: Hang in there.
: Welp! I’ll leave you two kids to it, then! I’ve got no job to do here and my presence will just be a bother!
: Hey, no. I really do want you to stay. It’s totally fine.
: Nope! I’m out!
: Don’t...do anything crazy without...calling your aunt!
Uta leaves just as quickly as she arrived.
Where she ran off to, I have no idea. But I guess this means that I have a little more time alone with Io.
: I really did want her to stay...
: She probably just felt uncomfortable seeing her friend cuddled up against her teacher.
: Probably.
: It’s admittedly not a thing either of us have any real experience with.
: Didn’t Uta think you were a boy when you two first started talking?
: Yeah. And I thought she was a boy too.
: But just because we thought each other were the opposite gender doesn’t mean we have any notable experience with said gender.
: It’s just weird that you make an exception to your “no girls” rule for her when she’s one of the girliest girls I’ve ever met. That’s all I’m saying.
: It is weird, yeah.
: But I really look up to Uta.
: She’s amazing.
: In what way?
: In that she got better.
: In that she can wake up and put a real smile on. And hold real conversations with all sorts of people.
: In that she can organize a classwide, two-day event on a whim and pull the entire thing off without so much as a drop of sweat.
: In that she’s pretty and sweet and doesn’t use that as a front to get what she wants from people.
: You clearly have not spent enough time at the maid cafe.
: That's a job. It doesn't count.
: Uta’s the perfect girl.
: I hate it so much.
: But I also love her so much.
: And I probably wouldn’t be here without her.
: And I’m not joking this time, by the way.
: I would very likely be dead if I never met Uta.
: She...seems like a great friend.
I’m not really sure what else I’m supposed to say to that.
Io’s always spewing out a corrosive mixture of positivity and negativity that blend just about as well together as bleach and ammonia.
The room fills up with fumes that my lungs can’t handle, and I slowly die with my hand still clasped around her shoulder.
: She’s the best friend.
: I just wish I could give her more than me, you know? Like, I suck. She can do so much better.
: Yeah, you’re pretty terrible.
: But you’re also great in your own ways too.
: Like what? Tell me some.
: Like...you’re light.
: You can lay here and I can’t even feel you.
: Uh-huh. And what else?
: That’s it.
: That’s all I’ve got.
: I can settle for that. That’s fair.
: It would probably be nice if you thought a little higher of yourself, though.
: I have to do something worthy of being praised for before I can even think of praising myself.
: Right now, I’m just a weightless, overmedicated cockroach with a grand total of two bras and four boxcutters.
: Why do you have four boxcutters? And why do you only have two bras?
: Do you want to buy me more?
: Bras or boxcutters?
: Why would I need three bras? I can just wash them.
: Why would you need five-
: You know, what? Nevermind.
: Just...do yourself a favor and...eat before you take your medication next time.
: I make no promises, Sensei. Sometimes, I just don’t want to eat.
: Well then don’t take your medication those days.
: Yeah, that’s probably an even worse idea than the not eating thing.
: Why do you have to be so difficult?
: Why do everyone’s standards for “easy” have to be so hard to reach?
: You’d think that “easy” would imply a complete lack of difficulty, but being easy to deal with takes a lot of work. Probably.
: I don’t know. I’m definitely not the right person to ask.
: I just hope that you're okay with me being the way I am, because I like this a lot.
: In fact, I like it so much, I’m gonna take a nap.
: Goodnight, Sensei.
: Goodnight.
I think about shooting some snarky retort at Io about how I wouldn’t have come here if she was just going to fall asleep on me-
But her forehead is basically a space heater right now.
And her body, despite being light as air, is the same way.
I’m flattered that she was able to carry on such a lengthy conversation with me despite showing all signs of not being well-
But not thinking about herself will wind up killing her.
In fact, thinking too much about herself will also wind up killing her.
Io is practically dead already.
And there is no one who deserves rest quite like the dead.
So I let her fall asleep.
And after she doesn’t wake up for the next hour, I carefully pick her up and lay her down on Uta’s bed, since that one is actually possible to reach.
And then I leave without checking the labels on any of her mystery bottles.
Io’s affection has increased to [io_love]!
